title: On‑Prem Fleet Safety Stock & Queue Scenarios (working)
body:
Purpose:
This working sheet captures an on‑prem (private/VPC) GPU fleet sizing approach that explicitly includes safety stock, queue/backlog scenarios, and procurement lead-time impact across regions. The goal is a pragmatic BOM + ordering cadence that protects latency SLOs under realistic failure and lead-time noise without overcommitting capital.

Scope:
- Regions: NA-East, EU-West, APAC-SE
- Workloads: low-latency chat (p50 < 120ms), high-throughput batch (embeddings)
- Models: 70B dense variant baseline; quantized variants considered for cost lane
- Time horizon: 18 months (quarterly procurement windows)

High-level assumptions (base):
- Avg tokens/sec per request profile (chat): 30 tokens/sec; avg response tokens: 120
- Average sequence length (generation): 350 tokens total per session
- Average concurrency per GPU (effective) at 80% util: 12 concurrent sessions (base model, FP16/AMP kernels)
- Token throughput per A100-80GB equiv GPU: ~1.6M tokens/hour (model-dependent)
- Mean daily GPU failure rate (unplanned): 0.03% (≈1 fail / 900 days per GPU)
- Spare hardware repair lead time (on-site replacement): 7 days median; replacement procurement lead time: NA 28d / EU 45d / APAC 60d
- Target fleet utilization for cost lane: 65% steady-state; latency SLO lane: 80% target with headroom for 95th percentile bursts

Scenario definitions (for planning):
- Conservative (planning for 95th bursts + 2x growth): demand growth factor = 2.0; target latency headroom multiplier = 1.6
- Base (expected): demand growth = 1.25; headroom multiplier = 1.2
- Aggressive (optimistic): demand growth = 1.0; headroom multiplier = 1.05

Sizing calculations (stepwise, textual formulas):
1) Baseline GPUs needed (steady-state) = ceil((expected_peak_token_rate / tokens_per_gpu_hour) * hours_per_peak_window / concurrency_adjustment)
2) Latency-lane GPUs = Baseline * headroom_multiplier (ensure integer round-up)
3) Safety stock GPUs = ceil( (daily_failure_rate * lead_time_days) * Latency-lane_GPUs + service_factor ), where service_factor defaults to 1 GPU per region for critical redundancy
4) Spare pool (cold) = round_up_to_rack_units( min(3, 0.03 * Latency-lane_GPUs) ) — keep at least 3 spare GPUs or 3% of fleet, whichever larger
5) Procurement order quantity per cadence = Latency-lane_GPUs + Safety_stock - existing_inventory_on_hand

Example numeric worksheet (Base scenario, sample region breakdown):
- Demand target: 2.4e9 tokens/day across customers (base)
- Tokens per GPU per day (A100-80 equiv): 38M (based on 1.6M tokens/hour * 24h with effective multiplexing)
- Baseline GPUs = ceil(2.4e9 / 38e6) = ceil(63.16) = 64 GPUs
- Latency-lane (headroom 1.2) = ceil(64 * 1.2) = 77 GPUs
- Safety stock (lead_time NA 28d, daily_failure_rate 0.0003): safety = ceil( (0.0003 * 28) * 77 + 1 ) ≈ ceil(0.6468 + 1) = 2 GPUs
- Spare pool min(3, 0.03*77=2.31) => keep 3 spare GPUs (round up to nearest full GPU)
- Total procurement target (NA region) = 77 + 2 + 3 = 82 GPUs

Region multipliers and notes (apply to base GPU counts):
- EU-West: +5% capacity headroom due to higher lead time fragility and customs delays; procurement lead time 45d => safety stock increases accordingly
- APAC-SE: +10% capacity multiplier for network egress/colocation differences and 60d lead time; recommend mixing 2 rack configurations (dense 8x GPU vs flexible 4x GPU) to reduce single shipment risk

BOM guidance (line-item sketch, unit counts are illustrative for NA procurement order above):
- GPU cards (A100-80 equiv): 82 units
- Server chassis (8x GPU chassis) required: ceil(82 / 8) = 11 chassis (+1 spare chassis) => 12 total
- NVLink/retimers/cables: 11 sets + 10% spare = 13 sets
- Motherboards/CPUs (per chassis): 12 boards; CPU spec: 64 cores dual-socket per chassis (TBD)
- Power distribution and PSUs: sized per chassis; recommend +25% headroom on PSU capacity; list per rack
- Rack count (42U standard): 12 chassis -> pack 3 chassis/rack => 4 racks (+1 spare rack for spare pool hardware) => recommend 5 racks allocated
- Top-of-rack switches: 2 x 100Gbps T0 per rack => 10 units + 1 spare
- Local NVMe (scratch): 8TB per chassis (enterprise grade) => 96TB total across chassis; procurement 12 x 8TB NVMe drives
- Kitting & spares budget: order +10% extra GPUs for long-lead replacements when lead_time > 45d (EU/APAC)

Cost placeholders (for handshake with finance; unit costs are placeholders):
- GPU unit cost (procurement quote median): $38k per A100-80 equiv (placeholder)
- Chassis + CPU + Memory: $12k per chassis
- Networking (ToR + cabling): $6k per rack (conservative)
- Rack + PDU + PDUs: $3.5k per rack
- Logistics / customs / duties: region dependent, assume 8% of HW cost (NA), 12% (EU), 15% (APAC)

Contingency and operational recommendations:
- Keep a rotating spare pool of 3 hot-swap GPUs per major region (not just cold spares) for immediate failover while repairs/procurement are in flight.
- Maintain a 2‑week cold spare kit for common replaceable spares (fans, PSUs, cables) per site.
- Define a preemptible capacity lane using smaller quantized model variants to absorb burst traffic and reduce incremental GPU count by up to 12% in base scenario (validate with perf tests).
- Use rolling quarterly procurement windows with overlaps: order cadence every 90 days but stagger shipments so that inbound lead times cushion to next cycle.

Failure-mode calculations (quick):
- Single GPU failure + no immediate replacement: if spares pool depleted and utilization >75%, expect p95 latency leakage; guard by safety_stock >= 1 per 50 GPUs
- Multi-site outage (region-level): route traffic to secondary region with routing policy; ensure cross-region spare capacity = 15% of aggregate region capacity for first 72h failover

Open questions / action items:
- Run performance sweep (applied-ml) to validate tokens_per_gpu_hour for the quantized 70B variant across target seq lengths (assign to Martin).
- Confirm current on-hand inventory for NA/EU/APAC (asset-ops) and feed into the procurement calculation (owner: Priya).
- Get three vendor quotes for GPU cards with lead-time estimates and confirm price bands (owner: Evan).
- Validate customs / import timelines per partner colo in APAC-SE (owner: infra-ops).

Appendix: quick formula cheat-sheet (copy into spreadsheets):
- tokens_per_gpu_day = tokens_per_gpu_hour * 24 (adjust for effective idle windows)
- baseline_gpus = ceil(total_tokens_per_day / tokens_per_gpu_day)
- latency_lane_gpus = ceil(baseline_gpus * headroom_multiplier)
- safety_stock = ceil((daily_failure_rate * procurement_lead_days) * latency_lane_gpus + service_factor)
- spare_pool = max(3, ceil(0.03 * latency_lane_gpus))

Notes on uniqueness of this doc vs existing artifacts:
- Focus is explicitly on safety-stock calculation tied to procurement lead time and region-specific spares distribution rather than pure BOM slicers or simple sizers.
- Includes queue/burst headroom multipliers and preemptible "cost lane" vs "latency lane" split that drives different GPU counts and BOM mixes.
